tldr: This is a research-theme thread, not one event: three weeks of independent arXiv papers on speculative decoding, from separate groups. Early work retargeted drafter training at acceptance length (D-REAL, REAL Loss), then the focus moved to block-diffusion draft trees and serving-side wins like grammar-forced drafts and KV reuse.
whats_new: DFly2 (Nov 25) drops the drafter's own KV cache and reuses the target's cache and sparse-attention selections, reporting more accepted tokens per step than DFlash and DSpark on long contexts.
why_it_matters: Speculative decoding is a near-free throughput lever in vLLM-class stacks, and these papers show the gains now hinge on drafter training, tree shape, and cache sharing rather than drafter size.

beats.headline: Drafters get trained on acceptance length directly
beats.summary: Token-level losses don't optimize how many draft tokens survive verification; four papers target that quantity or its proxies.

beats.headline: Block-diffusion and parallel draft trees compete on tokens per verify
beats.summary: Work builds on DFlash and DSpark, pruning or reshaping draft trees so each verification row banks more tokens.

beats.headline: Speculation moves into the serving stack: KV reuse, grammars, cache misses
beats.summary: Papers fold speculation into production concerns: invalidated agent KV, structured outputs, and long-context cache cost.

beats.headline: Other decoding papers clustered in by keyword, not by technique
beats.summary: These share the word "decoding" but address hallucination, fingerprinting, or recurrent-depth inference, not draft-and-verify.

open_questions: Does any of DFly2, DFlash, or DSpark land in vLLM or SGLang mainline with published throughput numbers?
Do acceptance-length objectives (D-REAL, REAL Loss) hold their gains under batched, high-concurrency serving?
Does Grammar-as-a-Draft's speedup on JSON and tool-call outputs reproduce on GPU runtimes, not just TPU v7x?
Does an independent benchmark compare the draft-tree methods (D3Tree, DForkTree, Pando, Corrective Prefix Attention) on the same targets?
take_for_builders: If you serve structured or tool-call outputs, benchmark grammar-forced drafting and draft temperature calibration on your own traffic before swapping drafter architectures; treat paper speedups as unreplicated.
